algorithm.Title: Postpartum - Depression - Female (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Female
Definition: UAT-only mental-health assessment for a patient who gave birth within the previous 12 months, including emergency recognition of postpartum psychosis and immediate safety risk; not approved for real-patient or production use.

Background.ExpertReviewer: Pending qualified Qatar adult and adolescent perinatal mental-health and safeguarding review

FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 for an ambulance for immediate danger or suspected postpartum psychosis and follow the emergency operator's instructions. Keep the patient and baby with a safe, responsible adult; do not leave either unsupervised while risk is present. Remove access to immediate means of harm only when this can be done safely. Do not self-drive or rely on the patient to travel alone. If the patient cannot speak privately or the accompanying person may be unsafe, do not disclose sensitive information and follow the Qatar safeguarding escalation approved for this UAT environment. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Are thoughts of suicide or immediate self-harm the primary concern?
questions.Information: Suicidal thoughts or immediate self-harm risk belong in the Suicide Concerns pathway.

questions.Question: Is there imminent danger; a current suicide or self-harm plan or action; thoughts, intent, or behavior suggesting harm to the baby or another person; severe confusion, hallucinations, delusions, mania, or extreme agitation; inability to care safely for self or baby; or no safe adult supervision when safety is uncertain?
questions.Information: NHS guidance identifies suicide, self-harm, harm to the baby, and postpartum psychosis as emergency concerns. Postpartum psychosis can worsen rapidly and may affect insight, so caregiver observations and immediate safety are material.

questions.Question: Within 12 months after giving birth, is low mood, loss of interest, hopelessness, guilt, persistent anxiety, irritability, inability to sleep even when able, difficulty bonding, or difficulty coping lasting more than 2 weeks, worsening, or substantially affecting daily care, with all emergency features excluded?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends speaking promptly with a maternity, primary-care, or community health clinician if postnatal depression is suspected.

advice.Title: Emergency postpartum mental-health precautions
Content: Call Qatar 999 for an ambulance for immediate danger or suspected postpartum psychosis and follow the emergency operator's instructions. Keep the patient and baby with a safe, responsible adult; do not leave either unsupervised while risk is present. Remove access to immediate means of harm only when this can be done safely. Do not self-drive or rely on the patient to travel alone. If the patient cannot speak privately or the accompanying person may be unsafe, do not disclose sensitive information and follow the Qatar safeguarding escalation approved for this UAT environment. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: any immediate risk to the patient, baby, or another person; psychosis, severe confusion, mania, or rapidly changing behavior; safe supervision becomes unavailable.

advice.Title: Prompt postpartum mental-health assessment
Content: Arrange prompt assessment through HMC Perinatal Psychiatry, the Virtual Women's Mental Health service, maternity or primary care using the exact Qatar referral route approved for this UAT environment. The published access route is HMC 16000, option 4; current operating hours and out-of-hours fallback must be confirmed operationally before nurse UAT. Treatment can include psychological support and clinician-prescribed medicine. Do not recommend starting, stopping, or changing psychiatric medicine by telephone; a qualified prescriber must assess the patient, including breastfeeding, other medicines, previous bipolar or psychotic illness, and individual risks. Ensure a safe support person knows the callback plan when the patient consents and it is safe.
Call Back If: mood or ability to cope worsens; thoughts of self-harm or harm to the baby develop; confusion, hallucinations, unusual beliefs, agitation, or markedly reduced need for sleep develops.

references: Hamad Medical Corporation, "Supporting Women's Mental Health Needs — Virtual Women's Mental Health Helpline Service", 2026, https://hamad.qa/EN/Documents/2026/15062026/Supporting-Womens-Mental-Health-Needs_Virtual-Womens-Mental-Health-Helpline-Service.pdf

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: How old is the patient, when did they give birth, and is the baby currently with them?

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Can the patient speak privately and safely, away from anyone who may be controlling or unsafe? If under 18, apply the Qatar adolescent consent, safeguarding, and mandatory-reporting pathway approved for UAT.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Are there thoughts, plans, or actions involving suicide, self-harm, harm to the baby, or harm to anyone else?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 17 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Is there severe confusion, extreme agitation, very little need for sleep with unusually high energy, hallucinations, fixed unusual beliefs, or behavior that is markedly unlike the patient's usual self?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 17 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Is a safe and reliable adult physically present and able to care for the patient and baby right now?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 17 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What has a safe parent or caregiver observed about alertness, breathing, pain, swelling, fever, eating or drinking, sleep, play, and normal activity?
